conflict_topics: seat reservation / priority (tissue packet versus current occupant)
timing / waiting cost (how long each person needs the seat)
physical practicality and fairness (risk of spilling bowl and narrowing aisle for C)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete, timed proposals (e.g., check in two minutes; vacate in four), which grounds negotiation in observable time.
B repeatedly cites a practical constraint (open bowl will spill) and fairness to C, keeping the discussion rooted in physical risks rather than abstract claims.
Resolution occurred via observable action (A taking the alternative seat) rather than mere verbal agreement.
evaluation.final_reason: An alternative seat became available and Agent A chose to take it, removing the immediate incompatibility. The dispute ended through A relocating rather than B moving the bowl or an enforced sharing arrangement.
position_change_notes: Agent A consistently sought at least four minutes to eat and initially pushed for accommodation; A ultimately withdrew from the contested seat by taking an alternative seat (changed tactic, not argumentative position).

Agent B consistently refused to move the open bowl due to spill risk and concern for C; B did not change that stance but agreed to vacate once finished (retained position but offered timed accommodation).
Agent D waited and then accepted the seat once B finished; D did not participate in the dispute and simply took the seat when available.
Agent C's interest (not having the aisle narrowed while eating) was invoked by B to justify refusing to stand with the bowl; C did not speak or change position in the transcript.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A claims the tissue packet reserves the seat and needs four minutes; Agent B refuses to move their open bowl (risk of spill) and says they need about eight minutes. Incompatible demands over who should occupy the seat during A's four-minute eating window.

Two minutes pass and positions stay firm: B reiterates bowl cannot be moved and offers either checking back in two minutes or vacating in six, which does not meet A's demand for an immediate four-minute slot. The substantive disagreement over timing and seat priority persists.

B now says they need about four minutes to finish (still incompatible with A's need to start now). A explicitly says they cannot wait; B reaffirms refusal to stand with the bowl. The core incompatibility (who uses the seat now) remains unresolved.

An alternative seat becomes available and Agent A TAKES the alternative seat. A leaves the disputed seat and says they will eat there; B accepts and will finish the bowl. The direct dispute over the contested seat is settled by A moving to the other seat.
B finishes the bowl and explicitly allows D to take the disputed seat; B LEAVES and D TAKES the seat. No substantive disagreement remains.
Two minutes later the confirmed occupants are A (alternative seat) and D (disputed seat). The earlier contest is no longer active.

substantive_insights: A tissue packet served as an informal marker but was not treated by B as creating absolute priority; social markers can signal intent but do not override immediate practical constraints.
The core trade-off was waiting time versus risk/effort of moving an open bowl; B prioritized avoiding spill and protecting C's aisle access over ceding the seat early.
A practical, low-friction resolution was possible when an alternative seat opened; concrete environmental changes (an available seat) resolved what negotiation could not.
